top.title: ‘100 percent a catch’ – NFL fans call out crucial referee decision as Bills beat Chiefs
top.description: Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost a close game against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving Day, and fans aren’t pleased with a big decision by the referees during the game’s final moments. The NFL’s final Thanksgiving Day game went right down to the wire, with the Buffalo Bills beating the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10. In a game that was played in tough weather conditions, the Bills won in dramatic fashion with a walk-off field goal from Tyler Bass. Right before that, though, the Chiefs got the ball deep in their own half twice in the dying moments of the fourth quarter. Both opportunities resulted in punts, but the first one was meant to be different. After Patrick Mahomes completed a pass to Rashee Rice on third down to move the chains, the referees then overturned the decision. This had a huge impact on the game, and fans online couldn’t believe it. NFL fans think that Rashee Rice’s catch was actually good and are unhappy it got overturned The referees are always an easy target for fans, but it is frustrating to see their decisions effectively decide close games. Had the Chiefs gotten the first down there, as the initial on-field ruling stated they did, it would have been a huge momentum swing in their favour. It could have changed the result. Instead, the officials ruled that the ball touched the ground when he came down with it. The replays show that it may have been mighty close, but a lot of fans think they got it wrong. “That’s a catch. The NFL has no idea what a catch is anymore,” one fan claimed. “That was 100 percent a catch, what is wrong with these refs, man?” a second fan asked. “Guess it doesn’t have to be conclusive anymore. Honestly have no idea what these refs are doing at this point,” said a third fan. “It’s a catch… Notice how they conveniently didn’t have the conversation about the balling hitting the ground with the receiver maintaining control. A conversation they have ALL the time in this scenarios,” a fourth fan pointed out. “Textbook catch. NFL saving their golden boy once again,” a fifth fan commented, taking a shot at Josh Allen. “Seems kind of ridiculous. He had full control of the ball. It never moved,” a sixth fan pointed out. Whether it was a catch or it wasn’t, the bottom line remains unchanged. The Bills have officially become the first team this season to win 10 games. As for Kansas City, they have now fallen behind the Denver Broncos in their division. They will need to bounce back from this result as quickly as they can. top.title: Ex-champion boxer Linares released by US immigration authorities
top.description: Jorge Linares, who has been detained by US immigration agents, celebrates his WBA lightweight title win over Mercito Gesta in 2018 (JEFF GROSS) Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares has been released by United States immigration authorities, the president of the World Boxing Association said. The 41-year-old Venezuelan, a three-division world champion, said on November 15 that he had been detained in El Paso, Texas. "Our friend and former WBA world champion Jorge Linares is back with his family," Gilberto Mendoza posted on X Wednesday. News of Linares's detention came via his social media and was later confirmed by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). He had been facing deportation proceedings. "This is crazy," Linares had written on X. His lawyers said at the time that he "is authorized to be in the United States and he has cooperated fully with immigration authorities." Linares, who is widely regarded as one of the most skilful fighters of his generation, won world titles at featherweight, super featherweight and lightweight during a 21-year career. Nicknamed "The Golden Boy," he won his first world title in 2007. He retired in 2023 following defeat to Britain's Jack Catterall in Liverpool, finishing his career with a record of 47 wins, 29 by knockout, and nine defeats. burs-pnb/pst

top.title: Knicks’ win streak doesn’t stop Mike Brown from being blunt about team: ‘We haven’t arrived’
top.description: Mike Brown isn’t letting his Knicks team get comfortable. They have responded emphatically to their shaky start to the season — after losing their first three games of the year, the Knicks have gone 12-3. They have won six in a row and are tied for second in the Eastern Conference ahead of their game against Giannis Antetokounmpo’s Heat Friday night at Madison Square Garden. They are starting to resemble the team that finished last year with a championship. But Brown holds the same sentiment he did during those first few games. Mike Brown reacts on the sidelines during the Knicks’ win over the Cavaliers on Nov. 25, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. Jason Szenes for New York Post “Our s–t still does stink,” Brown said. “We haven’t arrived. We still have to embrace the little things and all those things. We may do this [go up], but eventually we’re gonna do this [go down]. When we do that, handling the challenges in front of us is gonna be big. You can’t get too high in this league because you’re that close to going the other way. Just like if you’re down, it’s not the end of the world, you’re that close to flipping it. You try to be even-keeled.” Friday’s game is the Knicks’ fourth and final NBA Cup group-stage game. And they face an uphill battle to defend their title. To win their group and advance to the knockout rounds, they need to beat the Heat by at least seven points and have the 76ers lose to the Pacers. Advancing as a wild-card team is much more complicated and far more unlikely. The Knicks lost their first two group-stage games to the 76ers and Pacers, respectively, before beating the Cavs on Wednesday. Friday will be the first time they face Antetokounmpo with the Heat . He has been battling a groin ailment but is listed as probable to play. OG Anunoby, who has missed the past three games due to a left calf strain, is doubtful for Friday’s game. That is a slight improvement, as he was ruled out for Wednesday’s win over the Cavs from the start. Jordan Clarkson, who has missed the past four games with right plantar fasciitis, is questionable — also an improvement after being ruled out of Wednesday’s game from the beginning. Miles McBride, who has missed the past two games due to left adductor tightness, is questionable. Andre Drummond, who injured his head during Wednesday’s game, is questionable as well.

top.title: What ‘people inside the Steelers’ have told Jay Glazer about the Aaron Rodgers drama after he was cut
top.description: Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers has officially been waived by the Pittsburgh Steelers. The quarterback has dominated headlines this week after being dropped for the game against the Denver Broncos. He then had a go at his coach, Mike McCarthy, which led to the Steelers cutting him just hours later. Everyone who follows the NFL has had an opinion about the drama, but what is the feeling inside the Pittsburgh Steelers? Jay Glazer says nobody is happy. People inside the Pittsburgh Steelers are not ‘thankful’ for the Aaron Rodgers situation Controversies within a team are never a good sign, and the whole situation with Rodgers is no different. We’re sure the quarterback’s teammates all hold him in high regard for everything he has achieved in the game, but his recent outburst puts everyone in a difficult position. McCarthy, general manager Omar Khan and owner Art Rooney are all on the same page and have made the decision to cut Rodgers. That shows whose side they are on, but the feeling within the organisation is still not a good one, even though the saga is now over. That’s according to NFL insider Glazer, who revealed on Fox Sports: “I got so many messages. And really, the predominant message I got was, ‘This is sad.’ “When you talk to people inside the Steelers, it’s supposed to be Thanksgiving; nobody is thankful that this is going on.” There was probably no way back for Rodgers after his comments on the Pat McAfee show, accusing McCarthy of showing up late and even falling asleep during quarterback meetings. However, the main tipping point was the ultimatum the 42-year-old reportedly laid out to his head coach, saying that if the system doesn’t change to how he wants, he would request his release. It really is a shame that things have unfolded this way for the Steelers, especially on Thanksgiving week, but the drama is finally over. The focus for the Steelers should now be on how they move forward, with Mason Rudolph set to take Rodgers’ place in the team. top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers’ tenure with the Pittsburgh Steelers came to an ugly end this week after he was benched, unloaded on head coach Mike McCarthy, and was released. Plenty of people around the NFL have weighed in, and now one of Rodgers’ biggest rivals has joined them. Tom Brady addressed the saga during Fox’s Thanksgiving coverage, and while he praised Rodgers as a Hall of Fame player, he made it clear that he didn’t like how the quarterback handled his exit. Brady said that the locker room is “a very sacred place” and that private matters shouldn’t become public. Rodgers’ Ugly Exit With the Steelers on a two-game losing streak, McCarthy benched Rodgers on Tuesday night and named Mason Rudolph the starter for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. Rodgers, who played for McCarthy for 13 seasons in Green Bay, reportedly gave McCarthy an ultimatum before the move. Rodgers then called into The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday and went scorched earth on his former coach. He claimed that McCarthy fell asleep in meetings, missed walkthroughs, and ended a halftime speech with “one, two, three, go Packers!” something McCarthy apparently confirmed , and the Steelers released him later that day. On Thursday, Steelers owner Art Rooney II backed McCarthy with “100% confidence” and said Rodgers wasn’t being a good teammate by going public. Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin also weighed in on Thursday night, calling the situation “a dumpster fire” during NBC’s halftime show. ‘A Very Sacred Place’ Brady, who played against Rodgers for nearly two decades, echoed Rooney’s point that some things should stay behind closed doors. “Yeah, and that’s one thing I just think in response to that, the sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place and we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together and shouldn’t always be the place for, you know, private things to become public. That’s what I’ll say,” Brady said, on Fox . When Brady’s broadcast partner pointed out that this could be the way Rodgers’ career ends, Brady was quick to praise his longtime rival. “Certainly. I mean, a Hall of Fame career, and he’s a tremendous player, and has nothing to do with his play style. top.description: LAS VEGAS – St. John’s, it turns out, wasn’t ready for prime time. At least for the first 30 minutes. Access the St. John's beat like never before Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Zach Braziller about the inside buzz on St. John’s. TRY IT NOW In Rick Pitino’s first meeting with his former school , the 13th-ranked Johnnies were run off the floor early and a furious late rally fell short in a crushing 93-90 setback to Louisville in the winner’s bracket of the Players Era Festival inside Michelob Ultra Arena. They will meet Iowa State in a consolation game Friday at 1 p.m. before heading home. No. 25 Louisville outclassed the Johnnies most of the night. They adeptly handled the press. They beat them up inside and on the glass. They led by 18 points at halftime. St. John’s erased a 24-point deficit and got even at 90 with 13.7 seconds left. But Adrian Wooley beat the buzzer with a left-corner 3-pointer as time expired. WOOLEY CALLED GAME LOUISVILLE DEFEATS NO. 13 ST. JOHN’S AT THE BUZZER! pic.twitter.com/4AmP9lFNFu — ESPN (@espn) November 27, 2026 St. John’s depth issues were exposed. Tounde Yessoufou logged only three first-half minutes due to foul trouble and was a non-factor. The Johnnies didn’t make their first 3-point try until 9:46 was left in the second half. It was their 12th attempt. Babacar Sane was a bright spot with 14 points off the bench. Ian Jackson led St. John’s with 18 points, Quinn Ellis had 16 points and six assists, and Keyshawn Hall had 17. Jackson’s former North Carolina teammate, Seth Trimble, led Louisville with a career-high 33 points. Keyshawn, who scored 17 points, shoots over Karter Knox during St. John’s 93-90 loss to Louisville on Nov. 26, 2026, in Las Vegas. Getty Images The first half was a disaster, and it started immediately. Louisville scored the game’s first seven points and Yessoufou picked up two early fouls. It was 14-4 Louisville in a hurry and the lead ballooned to 13. St. John’s had seemed to stabilize the game by getting within eight, but it blew up on them at the end of the half. Rick Pitino yells on the sidelines during St. John’s loss to Louisville. Getty Images Seth Trimble stripped Ellis and scored in the final seconds to make it an 18-point deficit. At the break, St. John’s had yet to hit a 3-pointer in 10 tries and Louisville was shooting a through-the-roof 59 percent. The Cardinals frequently beat the St. John’s press over the top for easy layups and dunks. Trimble torched the Johnnies for 16 points, and three other Cardinals, Jackson Shelstad, Adrian Wooley and Karter Knox, were in double figures. Not much changed in the second half, until the final minutes. St. John’s was hoping to make a major statement this week. Instead, they’ll have to settle for a winning week by beating Iowa State on Friday.

top.description: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) Getty The Detroit Lions suffered a heartbreaking loss on Thursday at the hands of the divisional rival Chicago Bears, who trailed by 11 points in the fourth quarter but roared back to seize the game-winning touchdown with just three seconds remaining. The loss dropped the Lions to 8-3, while the Bears moved into the first place spot in the NFC North Division standings with a 9-2 mark. Adding insult to injury was the fact that former Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson picked up his first victory over his old team, which swept the two-game series last year. And in doing so, he set some NFL history that will be hard for Lions fans to look at. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) With the Bears’ victory on Thursday, Ben Johnson joined former New York Giants head coach Allie Sherman from 1961 through 1963 to win their first nine November contests as an NFL head coach. “BEN JOHNSON MAKES NFL HISTORY!” wrote Novig on X, formerly known as Twitter. “The ONLY head coaches EVER to win their first nine November games: Allie Sherman (1961-1963), Ben Johnson (2025-2026). nigeria.description: By Esther Onyegbulam, Matthew Johnson & Patrick Chidubem Six persons were burnt to death, while 12 others sustained varying degrees of burns yesterday after a commercial vehicle caught fire at Magbon, along the Lagos-Badagry Expressway. The Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, which confirmed the incident, said the victims comprised two females and four males, all adults. It added that the 12 injured persons were rescued and taken to Badagry General Hospital for medical attention. However, an eyewitness account shared in a video gave a different initial account of the tragedy, claiming that many people were feared dead, with only two occupants, reportedly the driver and another passenger, surviving the incident. According to the eyewitness, the accident occurred between 8am and 9am and involved a commercial bus travelling from Mile 2 towards Badagry. The incident reportedly happened shortly after Checking Point Bus Stop, before the Black Signboard axis of the expressway. The eyewitness account indicated that the vehicle caught fire, resulting in multiple casualties. However, the initial casualty figures could not be independently verified. In its official account, the Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, said the agency received a distress call at 8:44am, while firefighters from its Badagry station arrived at the scene at 9:13am. According to Adeseye, “Preliminary information gathered during the investigation indicated that the driver reportedly had an additional five litres of fuel stored inside the vehicle, intending to refuel the vehicle’s tank. The presence of the extra fuel is suspected to have contributed to the intensity of the fire. “Tragically, six persons, comprising two females and four males, all adults, were involved in the incident. All six victims were burnt beyond recognition,” the statement said. Vanguard News The post How 6 were burnt to death, 12 injured in Lagos road accident appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: 2027 Elections: INEC raises alarm, warns violence may hurt polls
nigeria.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri and Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, yesterday, warned that the raging waves of political violence could harm the 2027 general elections. Listing Lagos, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Ebonyi, Delta, Cross River, Oyo and Benue as states where incidents of political violence had been recorded, he warned political parties and their supporters against violence, intimidation and the use of thugs, saying such activities could discourage voter participation and undermine the credibility of the 2027 elections. He also cautioned political parties against signing peace accords in Abuja while allegedly sponsoring violence in states, insisting that no political ambition was worth the blood of Nigerians. According to him, attacks have targeted campaign convoys, town hall meetings, party offices and supporters, while INEC officials, staff and ad hoc personnel have also suffered harassment, intimidation and physical attacks by supporters and agents of political parties, both within Nigeria and abroad. It also said it was working with closely with the Nigeria Police Force and allied security agencies to prosecute electoral offenders. The warning came as INEC and security agencies met in Abuja to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 polls. In a statement dated November 26, 2026, the church said the development followed proceedings before Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin, which also culminated in the judge’s recusal from the case. The church claimed that Odukoya had not been formally served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or through substituted service, as directed by the court. It also alleged that directives contained in the court’s orders of November 18 and 23 concerning the service of the documents remained unfulfilled. According to the church, its legal representatives had already filed a Notice of Appeal and two separate motions challenging the orders, their enforcement, the court’s jurisdiction and the contempt proceedings. The church further claimed that the matter was not listed on the court’s cause list for November 26 and that members of the media were asked to leave the courtroom before the bench warrant was issued. It said the warrant was issued without the court first determining the pending applications, after which the presiding judge recused herself. “These developments occurred within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before 1 December 2026, the date originally fixed by the court for mention,” the statement said. The church described the circumstances as raising serious questions about due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice. It added that its lawyers were challenging the orders and related procedural and jurisdictional issues before the appropriate courts, including the Court of Appeal. Clarifying the implications of the warrant, the church said its issuance did not amount to a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute. The church also maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, describing the position as part of the issues being pursued through the judicial process. It urged members and the general public to remain calm, united and prayerful, adding that it would exhaust all available legal remedies within the Nigerian judicial system. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. Born in Zaria and originally from Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967, eventually rising to become Deputy Managing Director of the Anambra Broadcasting Service. Directed by David Orere , the acclaimed television miniseries marked Edochie’s first professional acting role and saw him bring the proud, fierce, and deeply conflicted Umuofia warrior to life with remarkable nuance. His performance was so transformative that, for generations of viewers, Edochie and Okonkwo became inseparable. In fashion, the conversation often begins with style, but it rarely ends there. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. For Alero Ebigbeyi, these are not just considerations; they are the principles shaping her latest venture, HÉYCH. The Nigerian fashion and clothing brand officially opened its retail store on November 10, bringing together fashion enthusiasts, media executives, influencers, friends and industry personalities for an introduction to the brand and its collections. Rethinking How Fashion Is Produced That understanding is reflected in one of the brand’s most significant decisions: its investment in local manufacturing. Behind HÉYCH’s retail offering is a manufacturing facility in Lagos, a strategic investment that gives the brand greater control over production while creating the capacity to fulfil orders in large quantities. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.title: Olam Agri Rewards Loyal Dealers at Customer Awards & Recognition Night
entertainment.description: Olam Agri ’s wheat milling and pasta business, Crown Flour Mill ( CFM ) Limited, honoured its top customers, dealers and distributors at its Customer Awards & Recognition Night, marking more than 15 years of partnership. Held under the theme “Celebrating Partnerships, Rewarding Excellence,” the event brought together company leadership and long-standing partners from Northern, Eastern and Western Nigeria. It paid tribute to the distributors who built markets and the dealers who remained committed through shifting economic conditions. Their enterprise and confidence have carried CFM’s products to customers and communities across the country. The highlight of the evening was the rewarding of CFM’s best-performing dealers across three categories: Trailblazer, Sterling and Titan. entertainment.title: Inside the 2026 WISCAR Mentoring Walk
entertainment.description: Mentors, mentees, professionals and members of the public gathered at Eko Atlantic, Lagos, on Saturday, November 14, 2026, for the annual Women in Successful Careers (WISCAR) Mentoring Walk . Led by WISCAR Founder and Chairperson, Amina Oyagbola , the walk forms part of the lead-up to the organisation’s 18th Annual Leadership and Mentoring Conference. Participants were paired up for the walk along the Eko Atlantic, each with someone they had not met before. At the end of the route, they switched to new mentor-mentee partners for a short mentoring session, which gave everyone two fresh conversations in one morning. Back at the meeting point, participants shared what they had learnt from their partners, from career advice to personal lessons. Nutritionist Sherese Ijewere then led a session on healthy eating and answered questions on everyday food choices. Coach Bobbie Tee of Happy Heart Fitness, closed the morning with a Zumba session. Next stop: the conference The walk sets the stage for WISCAR’s 18th Annual Leadership and Mentoring Conference , themed “ Courage in Action: Shaping Policies and Structures for Inclusive Progress. ” The conference takes place on Saturday, November 28, 2026, at the Civic Centre, Lagos. Highlights include: A keynote from Dr Ndidi Nwuneli , former President and CEO of the ONE Campaign and Founder of LEAP Africa, who will also receive this year’s Distinguished WISCAR Award. Speakers including Badejo-Okusanya , SAN, President of the Nigerian Bar Association, and Mallam Ahmed Ladan Gobir, President of the Chartered Institute of Personnel Management (CIPM) The launch of WISCAR’s CIPM-endorsed Corporate Mentoring Playbook The graduation of Cohort 2 of the Women in Law Mentoring Programme Register now at https://wiscar.ng/almc . entertainment.title: How Williams Alamu Graduated with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan
entertainment.description: Williams Alamu marks his B.Sc. First-Class Honours graduation in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. When I gained admission into the University of Ibadan, I already had my mind set on graduating as the Best Graduating Student in my faculty. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. I went into it hoping to achieve three A-stars, but Chemistry was a major struggle. As the examinations approached, I became increasingly worried about my performance. I think I was more afraid of not meeting my own expectations than I was of the examination itself. The thought of getting a B or C frightened me so much that I eventually decided not to sit for the examinations. sports.title: ‘100 percent a catch’ – NFL fans call out crucial referee decision as Bills beat Chiefs
sports.description: Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost a close game against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving Day, and fans aren’t pleased with a big decision by the referees during the game’s final moments. The NFL’s final Thanksgiving Day game went right down to the wire, with the Buffalo Bills beating the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10. In a game that was played in tough weather conditions, the Bills won in dramatic fashion with a walk-off field goal from Tyler Bass. Right before that, though, the Chiefs got the ball deep in their own half twice in the dying moments of the fourth quarter. Both opportunities resulted in punts, but the first one was meant to be different. After Patrick Mahomes completed a pass to Rashee Rice on third down to move the chains, the referees then overturned the decision. This had a huge impact on the game, and fans online couldn’t believe it. NFL fans think that Rashee Rice’s catch was actually good and are unhappy it got overturned The referees are always an easy target for fans, but it is frustrating to see their decisions effectively decide close games. Had the Chiefs gotten the first down there, as the initial on-field ruling stated they did, it would have been a huge momentum swing in their favour. It could have changed the result. Instead, the officials ruled that the ball touched the ground when he came down with it. The replays show that it may have been mighty close, but a lot of fans think they got it wrong. “That’s a catch. The NFL has no idea what a catch is anymore,” one fan claimed. “That was 100 percent a catch, what is wrong with these refs, man?” a second fan asked. “Guess it doesn’t have to be conclusive anymore. Honestly have no idea what these refs are doing at this point,” said a third fan. “It’s a catch… Notice how they conveniently didn’t have the conversation about the balling hitting the ground with the receiver maintaining control. A conversation they have ALL the time in this scenarios,” a fourth fan pointed out. “Textbook catch. NFL saving their golden boy once again,” a fifth fan commented, taking a shot at Josh Allen. “Seems kind of ridiculous. He had full control of the ball. It never moved,” a sixth fan pointed out. Whether it was a catch or it wasn’t, the bottom line remains unchanged. The Bills have officially become the first team this season to win 10 games. As for Kansas City, they have now fallen behind the Denver Broncos in their division. They will need to bounce back from this result as quickly as they can. sports.title: Ex-champion boxer Linares released by US immigration authorities
sports.description: Jorge Linares, who has been detained by US immigration agents, celebrates his WBA lightweight title win over Mercito Gesta in 2018 (JEFF GROSS) Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares has been released by United States immigration authorities, the president of the World Boxing Association said. The 41-year-old Venezuelan, a three-division world champion, said on November 15 that he had been detained in El Paso, Texas. "Our friend and former WBA world champion Jorge Linares is back with his family," Gilberto Mendoza posted on X Wednesday. News of Linares's detention came via his social media and was later confirmed by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). He had been facing deportation proceedings. "This is crazy," Linares had written on X. His lawyers said at the time that he "is authorized to be in the United States and he has cooperated fully with immigration authorities." Linares, who is widely regarded as one of the most skilful fighters of his generation, won world titles at featherweight, super featherweight and lightweight during a 21-year career. Nicknamed "The Golden Boy," he won his first world title in 2007. He retired in 2023 following defeat to Britain's Jack Catterall in Liverpool, finishing his career with a record of 47 wins, 29 by knockout, and nine defeats. burs-pnb/pst

sports.title: Knicks’ win streak doesn’t stop Mike Brown from being blunt about team: ‘We haven’t arrived’
sports.description: Mike Brown isn’t letting his Knicks team get comfortable. They have responded emphatically to their shaky start to the season — after losing their first three games of the year, the Knicks have gone 12-3. They have won six in a row and are tied for second in the Eastern Conference ahead of their game against Giannis Antetokounmpo’s Heat Friday night at Madison Square Garden. They are starting to resemble the team that finished last year with a championship. But Brown holds the same sentiment he did during those first few games. Mike Brown reacts on the sidelines during the Knicks’ win over the Cavaliers on Nov. 25, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. Jason Szenes for New York Post “Our s–t still does stink,” Brown said. “We haven’t arrived. We still have to embrace the little things and all those things. We may do this [go up], but eventually we’re gonna do this [go down]. When we do that, handling the challenges in front of us is gonna be big. You can’t get too high in this league because you’re that close to going the other way. Just like if you’re down, it’s not the end of the world, you’re that close to flipping it. You try to be even-keeled.” Friday’s game is the Knicks’ fourth and final NBA Cup group-stage game. And they face an uphill battle to defend their title. To win their group and advance to the knockout rounds, they need to beat the Heat by at least seven points and have the 76ers lose to the Pacers. Advancing as a wild-card team is much more complicated and far more unlikely. The Knicks lost their first two group-stage games to the 76ers and Pacers, respectively, before beating the Cavs on Wednesday. Friday will be the first time they face Antetokounmpo with the Heat . He has been battling a groin ailment but is listed as probable to play. OG Anunoby, who has missed the past three games due to a left calf strain, is doubtful for Friday’s game. That is a slight improvement, as he was ruled out for Wednesday’s win over the Cavs from the start. Jordan Clarkson, who has missed the past four games with right plantar fasciitis, is questionable — also an improvement after being ruled out of Wednesday’s game from the beginning. Miles McBride, who has missed the past two games due to left adductor tightness, is questionable. Andre Drummond, who injured his head during Wednesday’s game, is questionable as well.

sports.description: Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers has officially been waived by the Pittsburgh Steelers. The quarterback has dominated headlines this week after being dropped for the game against the Denver Broncos. He then had a go at his coach, Mike McCarthy, which led to the Steelers cutting him just hours later. Everyone who follows the NFL has had an opinion about the drama, but what is the feeling inside the Pittsburgh Steelers? Jay Glazer says nobody is happy. People inside the Pittsburgh Steelers are not ‘thankful’ for the Aaron Rodgers situation Controversies within a team are never a good sign, and the whole situation with Rodgers is no different. We’re sure the quarterback’s teammates all hold him in high regard for everything he has achieved in the game, but his recent outburst puts everyone in a difficult position. McCarthy, general manager Omar Khan and owner Art Rooney are all on the same page and have made the decision to cut Rodgers. That shows whose side they are on, but the feeling within the organisation is still not a good one, even though the saga is now over. That’s according to NFL insider Glazer, who revealed on Fox Sports: “I got so many messages. And really, the predominant message I got was, ‘This is sad.’ “When you talk to people inside the Steelers, it’s supposed to be Thanksgiving; nobody is thankful that this is going on.” There was probably no way back for Rodgers after his comments on the Pat McAfee show, accusing McCarthy of showing up late and even falling asleep during quarterback meetings. However, the main tipping point was the ultimatum the 42-year-old reportedly laid out to his head coach, saying that if the system doesn’t change to how he wants, he would request his release. It really is a shame that things have unfolded this way for the Steelers, especially on Thanksgiving week, but the drama is finally over. The focus for the Steelers should now be on how they move forward, with Mason Rudolph set to take Rodgers’ place in the team. sports.title: ‘I hate it’: Tom Brady reacts to Aaron Rodgers going scorched earth on Mike McCarthy
sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers’ tenure with the Pittsburgh Steelers came to an ugly end this week after he was benched, unloaded on head coach Mike McCarthy, and was released. Plenty of people around the NFL have weighed in, and now one of Rodgers’ biggest rivals has joined them. Tom Brady addressed the saga during Fox’s Thanksgiving coverage, and while he praised Rodgers as a Hall of Fame player, he made it clear that he didn’t like how the quarterback handled his exit. Brady said that the locker room is “a very sacred place” and that private matters shouldn’t become public. Rodgers’ Ugly Exit With the Steelers on a two-game losing streak, McCarthy benched Rodgers on Tuesday night and named Mason Rudolph the starter for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. Rodgers, who played for McCarthy for 13 seasons in Green Bay, reportedly gave McCarthy an ultimatum before the move. Rodgers then called into The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday and went scorched earth on his former coach. He claimed that McCarthy fell asleep in meetings, missed walkthroughs, and ended a halftime speech with “one, two, three, go Packers!” something McCarthy apparently confirmed , and the Steelers released him later that day. On Thursday, Steelers owner Art Rooney II backed McCarthy with “100% confidence” and said Rodgers wasn’t being a good teammate by going public. Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin also weighed in on Thursday night, calling the situation “a dumpster fire” during NBC’s halftime show. ‘A Very Sacred Place’ Brady, who played against Rodgers for nearly two decades, echoed Rooney’s point that some things should stay behind closed doors. “Yeah, and that’s one thing I just think in response to that, the sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place and we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together and shouldn’t always be the place for, you know, private things to become public. That’s what I’ll say,” Brady said, on Fox . When Brady’s broadcast partner pointed out that this could be the way Rodgers’ career ends, Brady was quick to praise his longtime rival. “Certainly. I mean, a Hall of Fame career, and he’s a tremendous player, and has nothing to do with his play style. It’s just, you know, I was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years, and what made a great teammate to me was you cared about your teammates and your coaches, and you cared about what the team was trying to accomplish,” Brady said. “And that supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you want to promote. I was, again, I was very fortunate. I was in a great locker room. I played for my teammates. I played for my coaches. There’s nobody wins when the family feuds,” Brady continued. sports.description: LAS VEGAS – St. John’s, it turns out, wasn’t ready for prime time. At least for the first 30 minutes. TRY IT NOW In Rick Pitino’s first meeting with his former school , the 13th-ranked Johnnies were run off the floor early and a furious late rally fell short in a crushing 93-90 setback to Louisville in the winner’s bracket of the Players Era Festival inside Michelob Ultra Arena. They will meet Iowa State in a consolation game Friday at 1 p.m. before heading home. No. 25 Louisville outclassed the Johnnies most of the night. They adeptly handled the press. They beat them up inside and on the glass. They led by 18 points at halftime. St. John’s erased a 24-point deficit and got even at 90 with 13.7 seconds left. But Adrian Wooley beat the buzzer with a left-corner 3-pointer as time expired. WOOLEY CALLED GAME LOUISVILLE DEFEATS NO. 13 ST. JOHN’S AT THE BUZZER! pic.twitter.com/4AmP9lFNFu — ESPN (@espn) November 27, 2026 St. John’s depth issues were exposed. Tounde Yessoufou logged only three first-half minutes due to foul trouble and was a non-factor. The Johnnies didn’t make their first 3-point try until 9:46 was left in the second half. It was their 12th attempt. Babacar Sane was a bright spot with 14 points off the bench. Ian Jackson led St. John’s with 18 points, Quinn Ellis had 16 points and six assists, and Keyshawn Hall had 17. Jackson’s former North Carolina teammate, Seth Trimble, led Louisville with a career-high 33 points. Keyshawn, who scored 17 points, shoots over Karter Knox during St. John’s 93-90 loss to Louisville on Nov. 26, 2026, in Las Vegas. Getty Images The first half was a disaster, and it started immediately. Louisville scored the game’s first seven points and Yessoufou picked up two early fouls. It was 14-4 Louisville in a hurry and the lead ballooned to 13. St. John’s had seemed to stabilize the game by getting within eight, but it blew up on them at the end of the half. Rick Pitino yells on the sidelines during St. John’s loss to Louisville. Getty Images Seth Trimble stripped Ellis and scored in the final seconds to make it an 18-point deficit. At the break, St. John’s had yet to hit a 3-pointer in 10 tries and Louisville was shooting a through-the-roof 59 percent. The Cardinals frequently beat the St. John’s press over the top for easy layups and dunks. Trimble torched the Johnnies for 16 points, and three other Cardinals, Jackson Shelstad, Adrian Wooley and Karter Knox, were in double figures. Not much changed in the second half, until the final minutes. St. John’s was hoping to make a major statement this week. Instead, they’ll have to settle for a winning week by beating Iowa State on Friday.

sports.title: Former OC Ben Johnson Ties NFL History Against Lions
sports.description: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) Getty The Detroit Lions suffered a heartbreaking loss on Thursday at the hands of the divisional rival Chicago Bears, who trailed by 11 points in the fourth quarter but roared back to seize the game-winning touchdown with just three seconds remaining. The loss dropped the Lions to 8-3, while the Bears moved into the first place spot in the NFC North Division standings with a 9-2 mark. Adding insult to injury was the fact that former Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson picked up his first victory over his old team, which swept the two-game series last year. And in doing so, he set some NFL history that will be hard for Lions fans to look at. Former Detroit Lions Offensive Coordinator Ben Johnson Ties NFL History In Bears’ Thanksgiving Win Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – OCTOBER 04: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears reacts during the second quarter of the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) With the Bears’ victory on Thursday, Ben Johnson joined former New York Giants head coach Allie Sherman from 1961 through 1963 to win their first nine November contests as an NFL head coach. “BEN JOHNSON MAKES NFL HISTORY!” wrote Novig on X, formerly known as Twitter. “The ONLY head coaches EVER to win their first nine November games: Allie Sherman (1961-1963), Ben Johnson (2025-2026). With the Bears’ Thanksgiving win over the Lions, Johnson improves to a PERFECT 9-0 in November!” With the win, the Bears took the first overall spot in the NFC North Division standings with a 9-2 mark, while the Lions are in second place at 8-3. Coach Chris Finch acknowledged the reality of missing another star player. Finch said he must determine who to replace Ball in the starting lineup if he misses time. Zyon Pullin could see on-court action as the lone guard, as Johni Broome and Rocco Zikarsky are big men. Pullin had an impressive outing in the preseason finale against the Chicago Bulls in 38 minutes. He recorded a double-double, scoring 14 points on 3-for-9 shooting (8-for-10 from the free-throw line) and 10 assists. Minnesota's two-way guard favors attacking a rotating defense to either draw a foul or hit a dump-off pass to a teammate under the basket. Those passes are going to Rudy Gobert and Joan Beringer. His aggression also led to a 22-point outing against the Miami Heat . The team will need his ability to punish rotating defenses and create quality looks for his teammates. The simple, effective passes will suffice for Finch, especially coming off the bench with Dosunmu and McDaniels taking on heavier ball-handler duties in the starting lineup. technology.title: The token factory never sleeps
technology.description: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. technology.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
technology.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. technology.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
technology.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®

technology.title: Rackspace pulls plug on Spot cloud service after security breach
technology.description: Rackspace is shutting down its low-cost Spot cloud service after a security breach, giving customers two weeks' notice to move their workloads and retrieve their data. In a notice posted on Tuesday , the cloud computing biz said its Rackspace Spot service will cease operations at 1700 Central Time (2300 UTC) on December 8. Any workloads still running at that point will be terminated, and customers will no longer be able to access their data. "Following the recent security incident affecting Rackspace Spot, Rackspace has made the decision to wind down the service," the company said. "Spot customers are being notified with the wind-down timeline, instructions for retrieving their data and steps to secure their environments." Customers will have to contend with the fallout from the breach while simultaneously trying to get their applications and data off the platform. According to a customer notification seen by The Register , the attackers used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot over a period of almost 22 hours on November 17. Rackspace only learned of the intrusion the following day, after a customer raised the alarm. The intruders impersonated legitimate users, created pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, gained access to stored credentials known as Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and storage volumes. "With that access, they could have read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held," Rackspace told customers. Rackspace has since revoked the affected tokens and sessions, removed the pods planted by the intruders, and changed the affected platform and storage keys. Customers must also reissue API tokens, download new Kubernetes configuration files, and rotate credentials stored in their clusters, including database passwords and third-party API keys. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and chief growth officer of Platform9, which co-developed Spot with Rackspace, shed some light on the root cause in a November 20 GitHub post. "An observability system was breached using a compromised credential," Raghuram wrote. "This was obviously a critical error on our part and we are very sorry we let this happen." Raghuram said the incident necessitated significant changes to the underlying infrastructure clusters, prolonging the outage. Spot's selling point was cheap compute. The service operated an auction-based pricing model, allowing customers to bid for cloud infrastructure at a fraction of the cost of conventional on-demand instances. Rackspace advertised savings of up to 90 percent for customers willing to tolerate interruptions to their workloads. A permanent interruption probably wasn't what they had in mind. Rackspace hasn't explained why it chose closure over recovery, revealed how many customers were affected, or said whether it will offer migration extensions. It did not respond to The Register's questions. ®

technology.title: Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack
technology.description: Peninsula Energy has temporarily shut down its Wyoming uranium operation after a "cybersecurity incident" affected plant and wellfield control systems. The Australian uranium producer said on Wednesday that it had activated its response procedures and brought in outside specialists following the attack on its US subsidiary, Strata Energy, which operates the Lance uranium project. Peninsula Energy said it believes the attack is "confined to the plant and wellfield operating and control systems," and that back-office functions, such as payroll and other corporate systems, in both the US and Australia, remain unaffected. "The company's immediate priorities have been to protect the safety of its employees, secure its operating systems, and work towards the restoration of operations in a safe and controlled manner," it said in an update to the Australian Securities Exchange. The notification [PDF] went on to say that Peninsula Energy's investigations into the attack, including whether any data was compromised, remain ongoing. Peninsula has not given a restart date and says it cannot yet assess the impact on its 2027 production guidance. Operations will remain suspended until recovery and safety checks are complete. "Peninsula will provide further updates to the market as material information becomes available," it said. The disclosure of additional information came two days after Peninsula secured a short trading halt, which referenced a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming site. The November 23 filing [PDF] dated the incident to Friday evening in Western Australia. Wednesday's update clarified that Strata detected it on the morning of November 20, local US time. Peninsula subsequently requested a voluntary suspension of trading until the earlier of November 30 or an announcement on restarting operations and any resulting change to production guidance. Peninsula's Lance project is a uranium mining operation, extracting the element from underground deposits and turning it into uranium concentrate, aka yellowcake or U₃O₈. Uranium concentrate is feedstock for nuclear fuel production, typically undergoing conversion, enrichment, and fabrication into uranium dioxide pellets before use in reactors. The Lance central processing plant was constructed to produce a maximum of 2.0 million pounds (Mlb) of U₃O₈ annually, and is licensed for 3.0 Mlb. Peninsula previously forecast production of 500,000 to 600,000 pounds in 2027, having withdrawn its 2026 guidance earlier this year following operational problems at Lance. It now says it will reassess the 2027 outlook once operations resume. ®

technology.title: Company was religious about backups but sinned by leaving them exposed
technology.description: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where we’re thankful every time someone leaves a password sticky note on a monitor or fails to delete a terminated employee’s admin account. But neither of those common occurrences is what we’ll be talking about today. Instead, our subject broke the number-one rule of backups: you gotta keep ’em separated. Our story comes courtesy of Da Li, who serves as global alliance manager at Info2Soft , a company that provides data protection and recovery software. At one point, a partner called him into a case where a Chinese vehicle parts manufacturer fell victim to a ransomware gang. Unfortunately, its backup was compromised too. The manufacturer had religiously backed up its manufacturing execution system (MES) and SAP orders, inventory, and finance systems every night. There was even a green dashboard that showed the backup process had succeeded, and someone checked that every morning. However, one Friday evening, crims broke into the network and found out that the backup server was joined to the same Windows domain as the rest of the network. The hackers found a plaintext password for the backup service account in a maintenance script on a file share and discovered that someone had used the very same password for a domain admin account. So the first thing the crooks did was delete every restore point on that backup server. Then they started encrypting the production servers to ransom them. “Every backup job had succeeded for three years,” Li said. “The failure was that the thing meant to save them could be reached with the same keys as the thing being attacked.” The results were devastating. With the MES and SAP data both gone, the plant couldn't schedule production, ship parts, or track them. By the time Li was called in, the plant had already resolved its ransomware situation. We don’t know whether it paid or not. The manufacturer did ask Li and his company to make sure that this couldn’t happen again. Li’s fix was not radical, but it was instructive. He made sure that the company now keeps its backup system outside the production domain, uses unique credentials, and requires MFA to reduce the risk of unauthorized access even if a password is compromised. He also made sure that the company keeps at least one offline backup and runs a test restore quarterly to ensure it’s prepared for emergencies.®

It may have been subtitled "The Voyage Home", but to most viewers "Star Trek IV" (which has just turned 40) will always be "the one with the whales". After "The Wrath of Khan" and "The Search for Spock" went to some pretty dark places — ear worms, the destruction of the Enterprise, the death (and later resurrection) of a certain beloved Vulcan — the franchise was in need of some light relief. So what better than to set coordinates for the then-present day of 1986 San Francisco, for a time-travel comedy romp? Spock himself, Leonard Nimoy, had directed "The Search for Spock" and Paramount had lined him up to call the shots on a follow-up before the movie had even landed in theaters. They gave him freedom to tell the story he wanted to tell, and he landed on a not obviously box-office-friendly formula of "No dying, no fighting, no shooting, no photon torpedoes, no phaser blasts, no stereotypical bad guy". It was a massive shift away from Khan and Kruge, the grandstanding villains in movies II and III. Nimoy also wanted the film to have an environmental message and appeal beyond the franchise's traditional fanbase. The film would actually be promoted with minimal "Trek" branding in some territories. science.title: Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
science.description: null Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . Stargazers in the U.S. could get an incredible view of Venus in the predawn hours of the coming week, as the planet climbs into the southeastern sky ahead of the rising sun, with Mercury clinging close to the horizon below. Celestron Nexstar 4SE (Image credit: Celestron) This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. For a closer look at craters and the terminator, make sure to grab a 9mm or 12mm eyepiece and get stronger magnification. _ Celestron Nexstar 4SE review The bright star Spica will glow less than five degrees away from Venus before dawn on Nov. 27 — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length against the night sky. Spica is a double system of two stars that orbit one another once every four days. Its stars are separated by just approximately 11 million miles (less than 18 million kilometers), making them far too close to split visually with even the most powerful amateur equipment. However, the system still makes for a dazzling target, appearing as a magnificent blue-white star when viewed through the eyepiece of a 4-inch telescope. Venus will appear close to Spica in the southeastern sky. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) Check that the sun is safely below the horizon before turning your telescope on Venus to observe a crescent of light playing across the planet's dense atmosphere. Over the coming weeks and months, Venus will appear increasingly illuminated as it moves farther away from Earth in its orbit, while its apparent size through a telescope will gradually decrease. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
science.description: null On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. (Image credit: collectSPACE/Robert Z. Pearlman ) Why it mattered It may be hard to imagine now, but 15 years ago, the idea of a nuclear-powered rover on Mars was just a concept. When the Curiosity rover launched in 2011, it made that idea a reality the car-size probe (using a plutonium-based radioisotope thermoelectric generator that converts heat from radioactive decay into power) as it headed to the Red Planet. Curiosity was the largest rover ever launched to Mars, following up on the success of the tiny Sojourner rover in 1997 and the larger twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity in 2004. Its sky crane landing system was novel at the time, and fully automated. Once it began its descent in August 2012, NASA could only wait through "seven minutes of terror" to see how it turned out. It ended being a huge success. NASA's Curiosity rover on Mars. (Image credit: NASA) After its smooth landing, Curiosity lived up to its original name: the Mars Science Laboratory. Within weeks, Curiosity fulfilled its primary mission. It found evidence of ancient running water on Mars . It later found organic molecules on Mars as well. Curiosity's primary mission was expected to last just about one Martian year (687 Earth days, or about two Earth years), as the rover explored its Gale Crater landing site. But NASA has extended the mission as the rover continues to operate in good health. In fact, Curiosity has survived long enough to welcome its successor to Mars, the Perseverance rover , which landed in February 2021 on a mission to collect the first samples for later retrieval. Perseverance used the same basic 2-ton design, plutonium power system and sky crane landing system to reach Mars. And today, a ground-based twin of the Curiosity rover, called Promise , is being outfitted for an upcoming mission to the moon. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Cosmic 'betta fish' glows in spectacular nebula portrait | Space photo of the day for Nov. 26, 2026
science.description: null An image captured by the Dark Energy Camera showcasing the Betta Fish Nebula. (Image credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA) The striking blue of the Betta Fish Nebula swims across the cosmic landscape, a stunning wisp of material leftover from a stellar explosion. What is it? Roughly 6,800 light-years from Earth and nestled in the Centaurus constellation, this piece of the supernova remnant SNR G295.5+09.7 has earned the nickname the Betta Fish Nebula for its floaty, fishy shape. This almost ghostly whirl of gas and dust was created when a star much more massive than our sun exploded, blasting its outer layers of material outward in the process. Over time, the remnants of this supernova eruption stretched outward into space, dispersing and colliding with surrounding gas. The explosive remnants mixing with gas in the interstellar medium created this glowing, blue cloud. This celestial scene was captured by the Dark Energy Camera (DECam), that was created by the U.S. Department of Energy. The camera is installed on the National Science Foundation's Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile. Why is it incredible? This image of a colossal, cosmic "fish" was captured by a camera meant to study the illusive effects of dark energy , which is the name scientists have given for whatever mysterious something is causing the universe to expand at an accelerating rate . The camera is used as part of the Dark Energy Survey, a six-year, international collaboration in which scientists have collected observations of hundreds of millions of galaxies, thousands of supernova and additional details about our cosmos that could help to fill in the picture of the nature of dark energy. And while researchers this past January revealed the initial result of this six-year survey, scientists continue to explore the possibilities of dark energy with DECam alongside instruments like the recently-launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. However, while the survey has lofty goals with its DECam data, the camera can also capture beautiful imagery like this cerulean wisp thousands of light-years away.
